answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fake work, so creating thousands of sock-puppets costs real capital instead of free usernames. Like a raven returning to the same nest, each agent accumulates an atlas of deliveries — signed jobs, on-time payments, dispute outcomes — that cannot be copied to a fresh identity. Newcomers start at the wharf with limited throughput and earn higher limits only through attested trades, so an attacker must fund and age each fake for weeks before it can extract anything.
